transcript.content: Hi, it’s good to meet you. What brings you in today?

I guess my mom made me come. I mostly just... I can't really make myself do anything anymore. I just sit in my room. I think I've had these same clothes on for a few days, I don't even know. I used to knit a lot, actually. I made this really long scarf once, it was like, mustard yellow, and I wore it all the time until I left it on the bus. The bus driver was this guy who always wore a Mets hat, and he told me he'd look for it, but he never found it. I liked taking the bus, looking out the window, but I don't go walking or anything like I used to either. I don't even journal anymore. And when my mom asks what's wrong, I just... I barely have the energy to even answer her. It's like, what's the point of talking, you know? My throat just feels tired.
Do you ever hear voices when no one else is there?

Voices? Um... no, not really. I mean, sometimes I hear people talking, but it's just the TV from downstairs. My mom watches a lot of game shows. The one with the big wheel, you know? I used to watch it with her, but I always thought the wheel was rigged. Like it always stops on bankrupt right when the person really needs the money. I won ten dollars on a scratch-off ticket once, though. I bought it at the corner store when I was getting... they have those little powdered donuts there. The ones in the crinkly bags. I haven't had one of those in forever. I don't really go out to the store anymore, so...
Before this current period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed and unable to do things like this?

Another time? Um... no, I don't think so. I mean, in high school I went to classes and did stuff. I wasn't like this. I took this biology class and we had to dissect a frog once. The smell was... it was really bad, that chemical smell. It just gets stuck in your hair and your clothes for the rest of the day. My lab partner, Chloe, she always chewed this really strong wintergreen gum to block it out. She gave me a piece once, but it just made my eyes water. I don't really like mint anyway. It tastes too cold, you know? I prefer fruit flavors, like those watermelon ones that come in the little plastic squares. But they always lose their flavor in like, five minutes, and then you're just chewing on nothing. It just turns into rubber. So I just stopped buying gum altogether.
Do you believe anyone is trying to harm you or control you?

Harm me? I mean... they're trying to ruin things for me, if that counts. Since I was taking those college classes, I've just known that the school portal and the clinic practicum people are doing it. They use these little wording changes in all their emails and in the assignment comments just to mark me as someone they don't want in healthcare. My mom says they're just regular messages, but she doesn't get it. She doesn't even know how to log into the portal anyway. She always forgets her passwords. She has this little green notebook where she writes them all down, but she can never read her own handwriting. Her handwriting is really loopy, like cursive, but messy. We had to learn cursive in the third grade. Our teacher was Mrs. Gable, and she smelled like baby powder all the time. She had this huge collection of ceramic owls on her desk. One time, a kid named Tommy knocked one over and it shattered into a million pieces. It was a brown one with big yellow eyes. I liked owls for a while after that, but then I watched a video about how they swallow mice whole and throw up the bones. It's called a pellet. We dissected those in science class, too, actually. Kind of like the frog. But they don't smell as bad as the frogs did. They're just dry and dusty.
Have you ever had a time when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or full of energy?

High or full of energy? Um... no, not really. I don't think so. Sometimes I'll drink an energy drink if I'm feeling really draggy, though. The ones in the tall cans with the textured grip on them. There's this pink one that tastes exactly like cotton candy. I used to get them at the gas station right down the street from my old high school. The guy who worked behind the counter there always wore these really weird bucket hats. Like, neon green or bright orange, indoors. He told me once it was because the fluorescent lights in the store gave him headaches. My mom gets headaches sometimes, well, migraines really. She just lies in her bedroom with the curtains drawn and puts a cold washcloth over her eyes. We have these blue washcloths, but they're getting all frayed at the edges. The threads just pull right out if you catch them on a fingernail. I actually need to cut my nails, they're getting kind of long and they keep tapping on my phone screen when I type. It makes this annoying little clicking sound. But um... yeah, no, I don't really get super energetic or anything like that.
Have there been times when you believed the school portal or practicum people were targeting you even when you were not feeling depressed?

Even when I wasn't depressed? Um... I don't really know. I don't think I keep track of it like that. They just do it whenever they want, because the portal is always up. You just log in and it's this really bright blue screen. It's actually the exact same shade of blue as my old winter coat. The puffy one I had in middle school. It had this fake fur around the hood, but the fur got all matted and weird when I left it out in the rain one time. My mom tried to brush it out with a dog brush, but it just pulled all the little hairs out and left these ugly bald patches on the hood. We didn't even have a dog, so I don't know why we had the brush. We had a hamster named Barnaby, but he escaped his cage and chewed a hole straight through the drywall in the laundry room. My dad was so mad because he had to patch it, and he hates doing house projects. He always gets that white spackle stuff all over his jeans, and it never washes out in the machine. It just leaves these chalky white streaks. But um... what did you ask? About the school people? Yeah, I'm not really sure about the timing of it all.
Have there been times when you were not feeling depressed but still believed the school portal or practicum people were targeting you?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? About the timing and the depression stuff? I really don't keep a calendar of it or anything. It's just... the portal is always there. It doesn't care how I'm feeling. It's just a website. Websites don't have feelings, you know? They just sit there on servers. I saw a documentary once about these massive server farms out in the desert. Just rows and rows of blinking lights in these huge, freezing cold warehouses. They have to keep them super cold so the computers don't overheat. Kind of like how grocery stores keep the meat aisle freezing. I always have to wear a sweater when my mom makes me go to the store with her, even in the middle of summer. Summer here is just so humid anyway. The air gets all thick, like you're breathing soup. My hair always frizzes up when it's humid. It gets this halo of little flyaways that just won't lay flat, no matter how much of that smoothing serum I use. The serum comes in this little glass bottle with a pump, but the pump always gets clogged halfway through. Then you have to unscrew the top and bang it on your hand to get anything out, and it makes a huge mess. It smells like coconuts, though, which is nice. I used to love coconut water, but then I got a bad batch once that tasted metallic, like pennies. So I stopped drinking it. But yeah... I don't know what else to tell you about the school people. I just don't really track it like that.
Was there ever a time when you believed the school portal people were targeting you for at least two weeks when you were not feeling depressed?

Why do you keep asking me the same thing over and over? I just told you I don't track it. Two weeks, three weeks, I don't know. I don't mark things down on a calendar. My grandma has this giant calendar in her kitchen, though, with pictures of lighthouses on it. Every single month is a different lighthouse. I don't really get the point of lighthouses anymore, honestly, because don't boats just have GPS now? My dad has a GPS on his dashboard, but it has this really bossy British lady's voice. She always tells him to make a U-turn whenever we pull into the drive-thru at Wendy's. I always get the spicy chicken nuggets there, but you have to specifically ask for fresh ones, or they give you the ones that have been sitting under the heat lamp for hours. They get all rubbery when they sit out. Kind of like pencil erasers. I used to chew on my pencil erasers in math class until the little metal part got totally flattened out and sharp. It tasted like metal and dust. I had this math teacher who always smelled like old coffee and peppermint, and he used to eat those little red and white mints right out of his pants pocket. They were always covered in pocket lint, which is super gross if you actually think about it. Pocket lint is basically just dead skin and fabric fibers. But um... yeah, no. I don't know if it was two weeks. I just don't know.
Do other people tell you that your speech is hard to follow or jumps from topic to topic?

Um, no? I don't think people say that to me. I mean, I talk just fine. I actually had to take this public speaking class in high school, and I passed it. Mr. Henderson made us stand up at this big wooden podium that had a massive scratch down the front of it, like someone took a car key to it. We had to write our speeches on those little lined index cards, but I always hated them because they give you the absolute worst paper cuts. Paper cuts are so weird, right? Because they barely even bleed, but they sting so much worse than a normal cut. Especially if you get hand sanitizer in them. The hand sanitizer they put in the dispensers at my high school smelled exactly like cheap tequila. My friend Jessica told me that, anyway. She actually got suspended for drinking behind the bleachers during a pep rally. Pep rallies were always so loud, the marching band would play the snare drums so hard you could literally feel it vibrating in your teeth. It always gave me a headache right behind my eyes, kind of like when you eat ice cream too fast and get brain freeze. I love mint chocolate chip ice cream, but only if the chips are those really tiny flakes, not the big chunks. The big chunks get stuck in your molars. But um... wait, what did you ask me? If people say my speech is hard to follow? No, I don't think anyone has ever told me that.
Do you believe you deserve to be punished?

Punished? No, I don't think I've done anything that bad to deserve punishment. I mean, my mom used to ground me when I was little, like if I stayed out past the streetlights coming on. Our streetlights were those weird orange ones that buzzed really loud when it rained. It sounded like a giant angry bee trapped in a jar. I caught a bee in a jar once when I was seven, but I poked holes in the lid so it could breathe. You have to use a nail and a hammer to poke the holes, but you have to be careful not to bend the lid or it won't screw back on right. My dad had this huge toolbox in the garage that smelled like oil and sawdust. He was always building birdhouses, but the birds never actually lived in them. They just built their nests in the gutters instead, which was super annoying because then the gutters would overflow every time it stormed, and the water would wash out all the mulch in the front flowerbeds. Mulch always smells like wet dirt and vinegar to me, I don't know why people put it everywhere. But um... no, I don't think I deserve to be punished. I haven't done anything wrong.
Before you started feeling this depressed, did you already believe the school portal people were targeting you?

I don't really know when the depression started versus the portal stuff. It all just kind of blends together, you know? Like when you mix too many paint colors together and it just turns into that ugly muddy brown color. We had to do that in art class in tenth grade. Mrs. Gable made us paint these still-life bowls of fruit, but the fruit was totally fake. It was made of that hollow plastic, and someone had actually bitten into the plastic apple and left deep teeth marks in it. I don't know why anyone would bite a fake apple, it probably tasted like chemicals and dust. Dust always collects on the edges of the ceiling fan in my bedroom. I try to wipe it off with an old pillowcase, but then the dust just falls all over my bed and I have to wash the sheets anyway. I hate doing laundry because the dryer in our building takes like three full cycles to actually dry anything, and you have to use quarters. Quarters get so heavy if you have a lot of them in your pocket. My grandpa used to collect those quarters with the different states on the back, and he had this big cardboard map where you pop them into the little slots. He was missing Rhode Island for the longest time. Rhode Island isn't even an island, which is basically false advertising if you think about it. It's just a regular state. But um... wait, what were you asking? Before I was depressed? I don't know. I can't really remember the exact order of how it all happened.
Did you believe the school portal people were targeting you before you started feeling depressed?

Like I was just saying, I really can't remember the timeline. Time is just super blurry to me. Blurry like when you go to the eye doctor and they put those yellow drops in your eyes that make your pupils huge and sensitive to the light. I had to get that done when I was twelve because I couldn't read the whiteboard in math class. Math was the absolute worst, especially geometry. Who even cares about the hypotenuse of a triangle? Triangles are a really strong shape though, I think that's what they use to build bridges. There's this huge metal bridge near my aunt's house that's painted bright blue, but the paint is peeling off in these big long strips. It looks like a giant blue snake shedding its skin. Snakes are totally misunderstood, you know? Everyone thinks they're slimy, but they're actually really smooth and dry. My cousin had a pet corn snake named Noodle, but it escaped its glass tank and we found it three days later curled up inside a winter boot in the hall closet. Closets always smell kind of weird, like old shoes and mothballs. Mothballs are so toxic, they look exactly like little mints but you definitely shouldn't eat them. But yeah, um... I really don't know which came first. The portal people or feeling down. It's just all mixed up together.
Besides the school portal, do you have any other unusual beliefs that other people say are not true?

Unusual beliefs? No, I don't think so. I mean, my beliefs are just normal. Normal is such a weird word though, right? Like, what even is normal? My mom always said it was a setting on the washing machine. We had this really old washing machine when we lived in our first apartment, it was this horrible avocado green color from the seventies. The seventies had the worst colors, everything was mustard yellow or brown or that weird green. My grandma still has a mustard yellow refrigerator in her basement. She keeps all her extra Diet Cokes in there. She drinks like six cans a day, which is probably terrible for her teeth. Teeth are so weird if you think about it, just these little bones sticking out of our gums. I had to get my wisdom teeth out last year and my face swelled up so big I looked like a chipmunk hoarding acorns. Chipmunks are pretty cute, but they dig holes all over the yard and ruin the grass. Grass is so annoying to take care of, you have to mow it constantly in the summer. The smell of fresh cut grass makes me sneeze really bad. I think I'm allergic to it, or maybe it's just the pollen. But um... no, I don't have any other beliefs like that. Just the portal stuff.
Was there ever a time when you believed the school portal people were targeting you while you were not feeling depressed at all?

I don't think so, I mean, I really just can't remember a time like that. It's like I said before, my memory of it is all just... smushed together. Smushed like a peanut butter and jelly sandwich at the bottom of a backpack. I used to always carry my lunch in my backpack in middle school, and my mom would put the sandwich in a Ziploc bag, but by lunchtime it was completely flattened. Ziploc bags are actually really bad for the environment, all that single-use plastic just ends up in the ocean. The ocean is terrifying, honestly. It's so deep and dark, and there are all those weird fish with the glowing lights on their heads down at the very bottom. They look like aliens. I watched a documentary about them once on a Tuesday night when I couldn't sleep. Tuesday is the most boring day of the week, it's not the beginning and it's not the end, it's just stuck right there. But yeah, I don't remember there being a time when I wasn't feeling depressed but the portal people were still there. I just don't know.
Have you ever believed the school portal people were targeting you during a time when your mood felt normal?

I mean... I don't think my mood ever felt normal when the portal stuff was going on. But like I was saying before, normal is just really hard to pin down. Like, normal body temperature is 98.6, right? I remember learning that in health class. The school nurse's office had this giant plastic thermometer hanging on the wall, but it had red liquid painted inside, not the silver stuff. The silver stuff is mercury, and that's super poisonous if the glass breaks. Mercury is a planet, too. It's the closest one to the sun, so it must be literally burning up all the time. I get sunburned so easily, I have to wear SPF 50 even if I'm just sitting inside by a window. People don't realize windows still let the UV rays through. My mom actually bought these heavy blackout curtains because the sun was totally fading the living room rug. It's this big rug with a crazy complicated pattern, it almost looks like a maze. I used to try and trace the path to the center with my finger when I was little. But um... yeah, no, I don't remember ever feeling normal with the portal people. It was all just bad.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the day nearly every day?

Sad? I mean, I guess. I'm not really sure if it's most of the day, every day... days kind of blur together, you know? Like when you look out the window of a car on the highway and all the trees just turn into this big green smear. I used to love road trips when I was little. We drove all the way to Florida once, and it took two whole days. My dad refused to stop for anything except gas. Gas stations always smell so strongly of coffee and those little rotating hot dogs. I don't understand how anyone can eat those, they look like they've been spinning there since the dawn of time. Time is such a weird concept anyway. We just made up hours and minutes to try and organize things, but really it's all just the earth spinning around. If the earth spun faster, would we age faster? I read somewhere that astronauts in space actually age slightly slower than people on Earth because of gravity or relativity or something. Space is so huge, it makes me feel like a tiny speck of dust. Dust is mostly just dead skin cells, which is really gross if you think about it too much. That's why I hate vacuuming. The noise of the vacuum cleaner is so loud, it makes my ears ring. But um... yeah, I don't really know about feeling sad all day. It's hard to tell.
Do you feel worthless?

Worthless? Um... I don't know if worthless is the right word. I just feel kind of... empty, I guess? Like a hollowed-out pumpkin after Halloween. We used to carve pumpkins every year on the porch, and my dad would scoop all the guts out with this big metal spoon. The seeds are so slimy before you roast them. We'd put salt on them and bake them, but they always got stuck in my teeth. I hate when things get stuck in my teeth, it drives me crazy. I had braces for three years in high school, and it felt like everything I ate got trapped in the wires. The orthodontist was this really tall guy who always smelled like peppermint and rubber gloves. Rubber gloves make my hands sweat so much. I tried wearing them once when I was cleaning the bathroom, but I had to take them off because my fingers felt like they were suffocating. Do fingers breathe? Probably not, but it felt like it. Anyway, I don't really know about feeling worthless. I just feel... not much of anything.
Has anyone ever told you that your thoughts seem jumbled or hard to follow?

I mean... maybe? My mom sometimes says she doesn't get what I'm trying to say, but she's always complaining about something. Like she complains about the neighbor's dog barking too much. It's a golden retriever, I think. Golden retrievers are supposed to be really friendly, but this one just barks at everything that moves. It barks at the mailman every single day at exactly 2:00 PM. The mailman wears these little blue shorts even when it's freezing outside. I don't get how his legs don't get totally numb. When my legs get cold, they get all tingly, like when your foot falls asleep because you sat on it wrong. I hate that feeling, it's like a thousand tiny needles poking you all at once. Needles are the worst. I had to get a flu shot last year and the nurse practically jabbed it into my arm. She had this big tattoo of a butterfly on her wrist. Butterflies are weird because they start out as caterpillars and then just turn into soup inside the cocoon before they grow wings. It's kind of gross if you think about it. But um... yeah, I don't know if anyone's actually used the word "jumbled." They just say I talk too fast sometimes.
Was there ever a time when you were not feeling depressed but still believed the school portal people were targeting you?

Not depressed? I... I don't really know. The school portal people are just always there, you know? It's like they're built into the wifi or something. Wifi is so weird when you think about it. It's just invisible waves flying through the air, going right through walls and people. I wonder if that's why I get headaches sometimes, all those waves just passing through my brain. My brain feels like it's full of static sometimes, like an old TV when the antenna isn't pointing the right way. We used to have this huge box TV in the basement, and you had to smack the side of it to get the picture to stop rolling. My brother broke his hand once because he hit it too hard. He had to wear this blue cast for six weeks, and everyone signed it with Sharpies. Sharpies smell so strong, it kind of burns your nose if you sniff them. I accidentally got black Sharpie on my favorite shirt once, and my mom tried to get it out with hairspray, but it just made a big smeary mess. Hairspray makes the floor so sticky if you spray it in the bathroom. But... wait, what were you asking? About the portal? I just... I don't know if I was sad or not when they started watching me. It's just always happening.
Do you believe the school portal people are targeting you because you are a bad person or deserve it?

A bad person? No... I don't think I'm bad. I mean, I try to be good. Like when I was little, I always tried to get those shiny gold star stickers from my teachers. They'd put them on the top of your spelling tests if you didn't get any wrong. I used to have this big purple binder that I covered in stickers, but the edges always started to peel up after a while. I really hate when stickers peel and the sticky part gets all fuzzy from dust and lint. Lint is so weird, it just gathers out of nowhere. Whenever I help with the laundry, the dryer trap is always full of this thick gray blanket of it. My mom says if you don't clean it out every single time, the whole house is going to catch on fire. Fire scares me a lot. The smoke alarms are so loud, they make my ears ring for hours. My ears ring sometimes anyway, just this high-pitched whining noise at night when it's too quiet. I have to sleep with a box fan on so I don't hear it. The fan has three buttons but the middle one is broken, so it's either barely blowing anything or it's like a hurricane in my bedroom. It blows my posters right off the wall. But um... wait, deserve it? No, I don't think I deserve it. I don't really know why they do it. They just do.

target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the item corresponding to my chief_complaint_symptom_code, which is S023.

patient.answer: I guess my mom made me come. I mostly just... I can't really make myself do anything anymore. I just sit in my room. I think I've had these same clothes on for a few days, I don't even know. I used to knit a lot, actually. I made this really long scarf once, it was like, mustard yellow, and I wore it all the time until I left it on the bus. The bus driver was this guy who always wore a Mets hat, and he told me he'd look for it, but he never found it. I liked taking the bus, looking out the window, but I don't go walking or anything like I used to either. I don't even journal anymore. And when my mom asks what's wrong, I just... I barely have the energy to even answer her. It's like, what's the point of talking, you know? My throat just feels tired.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there are psychotic symptoms independent of mood, specifically delusional beliefs, to distinguish schizophrenia/schizoaffective disorder from a primary depressive disorder.
doctor.question: Do you believe anyone is trying to harm you or control you?

target_item.name: Delusions
target_item.manifestation: Since I was in those college classes, I've known the school portal and the clinic practicum people were using little wording changes in emails and assignment comments to mark me as someone they don't want in healthcare, even when my mom says they're just regular messages.
target_item.reason: The doctor is asking if the patient believes anyone is trying to harm or control them, which directly assesses for the presence of paranoid or persecutory delusions.

patient.answer: Harm me? I mean... they're trying to ruin things for me, if that counts. Since I was taking those college classes, I've just known that the school portal and the clinic practicum people are doing it. They use these little wording changes in all their emails and in the assignment comments just to mark me as someone they don't want in healthcare. My mom says they're just regular messages, but she doesn't get it. She doesn't even know how to log into the portal anyway. She always forgets her passwords. She has this little green notebook where she writes them all down, but she can never read her own handwriting. Her handwriting is really loopy, like cursive, but messy. We had to learn cursive in the third grade. Our teacher was Mrs. Gable, and she smelled like baby powder all the time. She had this huge collection of ceramic owls on her desk. One time, a kid named Tommy knocked one over and it shattered into a million pieces. It was a brown one with big yellow eyes. I liked owls for a while after that, but then I watched a video about how they swallow mice whole and throw up the bones. It's called a pellet. We dissected those in science class, too, actually. Kind of like the frog. But they don't smell as bad as the frogs did. They're just dry and dusty.

doctor.intent: Determine whether there has ever been a period of elevated or abnormally energized mood suggesting mania, which would distinguish schizoaffective disorder from schizophrenia or severe major depression.
doctor.question: Have you ever had a time when you felt unusually high, euphoric, or full of energy?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about manic or hypomanic symptoms (feeling unusually high, euphoric, or full of energy), which is not covered in my symptom profile.

patient.answer: High or full of energy? Um... no, not really. I don't think so. Sometimes I'll drink an energy drink if I'm feeling really draggy, though. The ones in the tall cans with the textured grip on them. There's this pink one that tastes exactly like cotton candy.
